data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2016 the Syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding were GBP 1,157.9m. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle indicates a net prior-year adverse development (strengthening) of approximately GBP 61.3m (5.3% of opening gross claims), driven largely by movements on older accident years (notably the 2014 year). Management cite the Ogden discount rate change, a higher incidence of smaller-scale natural catastrophes and changes to reserving / deferred acquisition cost treatment as principal causes. The report also highlights an inherited GBP 15.7m loss via incoming reinsurance to close of the 2013 year and a post-balance-sheet Ogden rate announcement which further increased reserve requirements.
raw_causal_phrases: The Lord Chancellor's Ogden rate announcement, both in terms of timing and severity, has overshadowed our 2016 results.
increases in reserves within our motor reinsurance and general liability classes have significantly eroded profits this year
an increased prevalence of global natural disasters
Included within the loss is an increase in reserves of GBP 33.1 million on 2014 and prior underwriting years
In 2016, the managing agent reviewed the Syndicate's accounting policy relating to the treatment of deferred acquisition costs
The revision of the Ogden rate from 2.5% to minus 0.75% has resulted in a material impact to the result of the Syndicate
data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development gross figure was not stated explicitly in a single 'movement in prior year's provision' gross line. The prior-year strengthening (+61.3m) is calculated from the gross claims development triangle (gross cumulative estimates diagonal comparison) and therefore is a calculated gross figure. The Managing Agent narrative and P&L refer to a net prior-year increase of GBP 33.1m (net of reinsurance). An incoming RITC (2013 year) of GBP 15.7m is explicitly mentioned and may distort comparisons; Ogden rate change was announced post-balance-sheet (27 Feb 2017) and materially impacted reserves but its full GBP impact is not disaggregated in the accounts.
